warnings: task_input_warnings carried forward: source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic; extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify extraction schema is mapped to influenza fields before collection
The target time window (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) corresponds to CDC Epidemiological Week 40 (EW40) of the 2024-2025 influenza season — use EW40 as a primary query anchor
Early-season influenza activity in the US is typically low in EW40; data may be sparse or show 'minimal/sporadic' activity levels rather than discrete case counts

CDC FluView for EW40 2024 would typically be published approximately one week after the week ends (around 2024-10-11) — there may be a reporting lag affecting data availability within the stated window
Avian influenza (H5N1) human cases in the US were being reported in 2024 — strictly exclude these from seasonal influenza collection; they require a separate disease profile
Do not conflate influenza vaccination coverage reports with case/outbreak data
Some state health departments may not publish weekly influenza reports until flu season is declared active — data gaps at state level are expected for this early-season window
Evidence quotes must capture numeric values, geographic scope, time period, and case classification type to be auditable

iterative_source_discovery_summary.stop_reason: Max iterations (2) reached. The primary CDC FluView Week 40 2024 source is confirmed in the result set. State-level sources (Mississippi, New York, Florida, Illinois, Wisconsin) and international/news sources appeared in iteration 2 results. No additional search iterations are possible or warranted.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Core coverage is adequate for the task window. The CDC FluView Week 40 2024 report (ending Oct 5, 2024) is the definitive national-level source and was confirmed in iteration 1. The Mississippi MSDH PDF explicitly covers Sept. 29–Oct. 5, 2024 with ILI rate data. Iteration 2 surfaced additional state-level domains (health.ny.gov, floridahealth.gov, dph.illinois.gov, slh.wisc.edu) and PAHO results (×4), plus news sources (Reuters, NBC, ABC, CIDRAP). The FluSurv-NET overview page was retrieved but is a methodology page, not a week-specific data page — week 40 hospitalization rates would need to be extracted from FluView Interactive. The WHO result retrieved (cdn.who.int update #466) is dated March 2024, not October 2024, so it does not cover the task window; however, PAHO results (×4) may include relevant October 2024 regional bulletins. Overall, national and subnational coverage is sufficient for the target fields given the early-season, low-activity nature of Week 40 2024.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources dominate: CDC FluView (cdc.gov) is the gold standard for U.S. influenza surveillance. MSDH (msdh.ms.gov) is an official state .gov source with explicit week 40 2024 date range. PAHO (paho.org) is an authoritative international organization. State .gov domains (health.ny.gov, floridahealth.gov, dph.illinois.gov) are official. CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a reputable academic public health news source. Reuters and NBC/ABC are credible mainstream news outlets. The WHO cdn.who.int result is a March 2024 update (wrong time window) and should not be used as evidence for October 2024. The Facebook/AAP post and familiesfightingflu.org are season-level, not week-specific, and should be treated as secondary corroboration only. The nnph.org Week 10 2024-2025 PDF covers a different week (Week 10, not Week 40) and should not be used for the task window.
